rules.threshold_text: no large-load class or threshold in the tariff (service class by Character of Service); the report's large load inventory counts grid connections greater than 10 MW
rules.collateral: financial security posted when a construction contract or other agreement is executed; a contribution covering the customer's portion of system reinforcement, refundable or non-refundable (refundable deposits, non-refundable deposits, CIAC or a facilities charge) under General Information Section 26 of PSC No. 15; non-refundable funds where projected revenue does not offset the cost
rules.exit_fee: on cancellation by the customer, costs incurred are retained from any posted deposit and unspent funds returned; no exit fee printed
rules.study_timeline: impact studies for projects outside the NYISO process: generally about 4 to 6 months

rules.utility: Consolidated Edison Company of New York, Inc.
rules.threshold_text: transmission: NYISO Load Interconnection Procedures for loads greater than 10 MW at 115 kV or above, or 80 MW or more below 115 kV; distribution: requests of 10 MW or greater get a service determination (low or high tension); large commercial customers are served under SC 9
rules.collateral: transmission: security posted after the Facilities Study identifies the costs; distribution: where construction cost attributable to the new service exceeds $2M, CIAC of the lesser of the cost above $2M or the cost less five times estimated annual Pure Base Revenue; Rider Y: an Excess Facilities Amount for high load-density service; any tariff cost must be paid in full before Company field work
rules.exit_fee: on cancellation, the customer's financial security is applied to outstanding obligations, including incurred costs of assigned upgrades; no exit fee printed
rules.study_timeline: distribution: for more standard requests for service, a target of 30 days for major project load service determinations and feeder concurrence studies (averages 35 and 32 days); large load requests can require additional review time when area station impact studies and complex distribution system analyses are needed; transmission: no stated stage timelines (NYISO process)

rules.utility: Consolidated Edison Company of New York; Orange and Rockland Utilities; Niagara Mohawk Power Corporation (National Grid); New York State Electric & Gas; Rochester Gas and Electric; Central Hudson Gas & Electric (New York's PSC-regulated electric utilities)
rules.collateral: current practice across the transmission owners: customers fund project-specific facility upgrades and provide financial security (letters of credit, bonds, parent guarantees or cash) before the utility commits significant resources or incurs construction costs
rules.exit_fee: current practice: on cancellation, costs already incurred are retained from deposits and unspent funds returned; no exit fee printed
rules.study_timeline: current practice: NYISO-jurisdictional projects, System Impact Study about 6 to 12 months and Facility Study about 6 to 15 months for lower-complexity projects; projects in a utility's local jurisdiction, capacity study then load study, generally 1 to 6 months overall

rules.utility: Long Island Power Authority (LIPA), served by PSEG Long Island
rules.threshold_text: Large Load Facilities: Maximum Gross Demand of 20 MW or greater (Performance Requirements apply); review thresholds 1.5 MW, 20 MW and 40 MW; loads of 40 MW or greater must connect to the transmission system; Interconnection Agreement for service at or above 23 kV
rules.collateral: transmission-connected loads pay all costs of their request, including transmission upgrades, and must sign the agreements and meet financial security or deposit obligations before significant utility spending; distribution-connected loads pay for dedicated facilities
rules.exit_fee: no exit fee printed; on cancellation the customer is generally responsible for study costs incurred on its behalf; costs already incurred for completed engineering, planning, procurement or construction are typically not refundable; transmission-connected customers remain responsible for the costs created by their request, including transmission upgrades already initiated
rules.study_timeline: typical: distribution assessment about 3 months; System Impact Study about 6 to 9 months; Facilities Study about 180 days (project-specific; actual large load studies can run well beyond a year)

rules.utility: New York State Electric & Gas Corporation (NYSEG) and Rochester Gas and Electric Corporation (RG&E)
rules.threshold_text: no large-load class (NYSEG SC 7-4 transmission or SC 7-2 primary; RG&E SC 8); the companies' Large Load Project Tracker covers projects over 10 MW at 115 kV or above and over 80 MW below 115 kV
rules.collateral: customer-specific facilities funded 100 percent by the customer, with prepayment; financial security as a bond, letter of credit, parent guarantee or cash once the customer agrees to costs and payment schedules
rules.exit_fee: no exit fee printed; contract terms assign default or termination costs to the customer; upgrades of an abandoned project stay with the companies or are removed at the customer's expense
rules.study_timeline: NYISO-jurisdictional: System Impact Study 8 to 12 months; Facility Study about 11 months for a low-complexity project; agreement negotiation 3 to 6 months; non-NYISO projects: study 1 to 6 months; cost estimates expire after 6 months

rules.utility: Niagara Mohawk Power Corporation d/b/a National Grid
rules.threshold_text: no large-load class: large retail customers may be served under an existing large general service class; the report covers transmission-connected requests of 10 MW or greater
rules.collateral: customer-funded preliminary assessments, NYISO study deposits and preliminary engineering (Support Services Arrangements); CIAC for attributable facilities due before utility capital outlays, or revenue assurance supported by minimum contract demand and an irrevocable letter of credit
rules.exit_fee: no exit fee printed; the irrevocable letter of credit covers a customer that does not connect after construction, fails to pay, or closes before the end of the agreement term
rules.study_timeline: indicative: early engagement and planning 1 to 3 months; NYISO System Impact Study 6 to 12 months; Facility Study 9 to 15 months (planning ranges, not commitments)

rules.threshold_text: no large-load threshold of O&R's own: projects meeting NYISO thresholds go to the NYISO process; commercial customers with a minimum demand over 1,000 kW at primary or transmission voltage are served under SC 9, industrial under SC 22
rules.collateral: customer pays application fees, study costs, required deposits, customer-specific facilities and system upgrades, as the agreements specify; 100 percent of facilities and upgrades needed exclusively for its interconnection
rules.exit_fee: on cancellation, the customer's financial security is applied to outstanding obligations, including incurred costs of assigned upgrades (stated for both companies); no exit fee printed
rules.study_timeline: local process: System Impact Study typically 4 to 8 months, then Facilities Study typically 6 to 12 months; NYISO-jurisdictional projects follow NYISO's procedures

queue_totals.utility: Consolidated Edison Company of New York; Orange and Rockland Utilities; Niagara Mohawk Power Corporation (National Grid); New York State Electric & Gas; Rochester Gas and Electric; Central Hudson Gas & Electric (New York's PSC-regulated electric utilities)
queue_totals.figure: nearly 14 GW of large load requests in the NYISO interconnection queue as of September 2026, over 8 GW of it entering in 2025 (statewide; each utility's own inventory is on its row)
4 projects over 10 MW since 2022, about 290 MW of requested peak load, none interconnected (inventory reported to the DPS); as reported in Appendix A of the DPS report, which prints no as-of date

queue_totals.utility: Consolidated Edison Company of New York, Inc.
queue_totals.figure: distribution: 48 large load projects proposed 2022 to present, about 864 MW (12 cancelled, 1 complete, 31 in design, 4 in construction); transmission: 3 projects totaling about 1,216 MW (1,000 MW, 200 MW, and a 16.5 MW project withdrawn); as reported in Appendix B of the DPS report, which prints no as-of date

5 large load projects proposed to connect to the transmission system 2022 to present, about 236 MW of peak load (4 in design pending the Interconnection Agreement, 1 cancelled); as reported in Appendix B of the DPS report, which prints no as-of date

queue_totals.utility: Niagara Mohawk Power Corporation d/b/a National Grid
queue_totals.figure: about 55 large load projects, about 7,792 MW of requested demand, as of September 2026: 20 in the NYISO queue (2,992.2 MW) and 35 prospective projects not yet in it (4,800 MW)

queue_totals.figure: 36 large (10 MW+) load projects: 12 NYISO-jurisdictional (2,460 MW) and 24 non-NYISO (560 MW); 10 cancelled, 2 in service, the rest in study; as reported in Appendix F of the DPS report, which prints no as-of date
